Heard learned counsel for the petitioners; learned High Court Government Pleader for the State and learned counsel for Respondent No.5.
2.

This Petition is filed by the petitioners seeking a writ of mandamus for a direction to the respondents to consider the representations dated 22.8.2019 vide Annexures-G1 to G5.
3.
It is the case of the petitioners that originally one Shah Shamsuddin Kunjenasheen was the owner in possession of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:8555 land bearing Sy.No.15/1/A, totally measuring 9 acres.

Out of the said land, 4 acres 20 guntas was purchased by husband of the 1st petitioner by way of Sumitra Bai And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181977431/
2 registered sale deed dated 3.4.1981.

entities.text: Sumitra Bai And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pursuant to the death of husband of the 1st petitioner, the name of 1st petitioner came to be entered in the revenue records and she is in possession and enjoyment of the said land and the Record of Rights show the entries of the 1st petitioner.

Similarly, 2nd petitioner also purchased portion of the said land to an extent of 4 acres 20 guntas, who is none other than son of the 1st petitioner vide registered sale deed dated 3.4.1981 and revenue entries changed in the name of the 2nd petitioner.

4. It is further case of the petitioners that portion of the said lands were acquired for formation of Chidri Ring Road in the year 2010 and infact the respondents have utilized an extent of 1200 feet x 80 feet (East-West - 1200 feet and North-South 80 feet), out of 4 acres 11 guntas and 4 acres 17 guntas in Sy.No.15/1A1 without issuance of any notice or initiating any acquisition proceedings as per the Land Acquisition Act.
At the time of laying the road in the land of the petitioners, the respondents assured that the compensation NC: 2023:KHC-K:8555 would be paid.
Till date, no compensation is paid for acquiring of the lands belonging to the petitioners.
The petitioners made several representations to the respondents to pay compensation for acquiring and utilizing the lands belonging to them and the same were not considered.

5. Being aggrieved by the inaction of the respondents in not paying compensation for having acquired lands of the petitioners, they made representations dated 22.8.2019 to the respondents vide Annexure-G1 to G5 seeking to pay compensation.
In view of non-consideration of said representations, the petitioners are before this Court by way of this writ petition.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioners reiterating the averments made in the petition seeks for a writ of mandamus for a direction to the respondents to consider the representations dated 22.8.2019 vide Annexure-G1 to G5.
7.
Per contra, learned HCGP submits that the Petition deserves to be dismissed as devoid of merits.

Even according to the petitioners, the road has been formed in the year 2010, but till filing of this petition in the year 2019, the petitioners NC: 2023:KHC-K:8555 have not taken any action seeking compensation and belatedly made representations on 22.8.2019.
8.

Be that as it may, if the lands of the petitioners are acquired by the respondents for formation of the road as alleged, the respondents are duty bound to act in accordance with law as they are State and Agency of the State.
It is also not forthcoming as to whether the representations dated 22.8.2019 have been considered and whether any compensation is paid.

It is trite law when any property of the citizen of this country is acquired or taken away by the State or any agency of the State or Public body, they are duty bound to pay the compensation to the aggrieved persons, in accordance with law.

9. In view of the above, I deem it appropriate to pass the following:
ORDER

A writ of mandamus is issued directing the Respondent nos.2 and 5 to consider the representations filed by the petitioners dated 22.8.2019 vide Annexures-G2 and G5 and pass suitable orders in accordance with law within an Sumitra Bai And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181977431/
3 outer NC: 2023:KHC-K:8555 limit of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
Sd/-
